crypto-macro.h3: Warsh warns the Fed still has work to do on inflation
crypto-macro.summary: The Fed chair used his Jackson Hole keynote to put prices first, sending September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to about 60% in a single day.
body: 65 months of sustained elevated inflation sit squarely with the central bank, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said in his keynote at the Kansas City Fed symposium on 28 August. He said the Fed must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to the 2% objective clearly and at sufficient speed, and that otherwise there is work to do.

Rate markets repriced within minutes. The two-year Treasury yield rose about 12 basis points to 4.35% and odds of a hike at the 16 September FOMC meeting jumped to roughly 60% from about 35% the day before. Warsh had been expected to use the venue to prepare markets for a policy shift.

Bitcoin fell from an overnight high above $81,000 to below $78,000 during the session, and crypto-linked equities were hit hard. Strategy lost 6.5%, Coinbase 5.4%, Galaxy 6.7%, Circle 5.5% and Hut 8 8%.

crypto-macro.h3: Hammack repeats her call for an immediate rate hike
crypto-macro.summary: The Cleveland Fed president said it is time to raise rates and expects inflation to end 2026 near 3%.
body: 3% is where Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack expects inflation to finish the year, a full point above the Federal Reserve target. She said on 28 August, hours before Warsh took the stage in Jackson Hole, that the central bank should hike now.

Hammack was one of three regional Fed presidents who dissented at the July meeting in favour of higher rates, alongside Neel Kashkari of Minneapolis and Lorie Logan of Dallas. The committee held the federal funds target at 3.50% to 3.75% by a 9 to 3 vote, the fifth straight meeting of 2026 without a move.
Earlier on Friday the CME FedWatch tool still showed a 58% chance of no change in September. That flipped after the keynote.

crypto-macro.h3: July PCE holds at 3.7% with core stuck at 3.3%
crypto-macro.summary: The Fed preferred inflation gauge came in slightly hotter than forecast on 26 August, with core unchanged for a fourth month.
body: 3.7% was the annual pace of headline PCE inflation in July, unchanged from June and above the 3.6% economists had expected. The Bureau of Economic Analysis published the figures on 26 August.

Core PCE, which strips out food and energy, rose 0.2% on the month and 3.3% on the year, in line with forecasts. Core readings of 3.3% in April, 3.4% in May, 3.3% in June and 3.3% again in July leave almost no net improvement across four months.
Personal income rose 0.4% and spending rose 0.2%, both stronger than expected. Headline PCE has eased from a three-year peak in May but remains well above the 2% target.

crypto-macro.h3: Benchmark revision erases 79,000 US jobs
crypto-macro.summary: The BLS preliminary revision cut job growth in the year to March 2026 while August consumer sentiment fell again.
body: 79,000 fewer jobs were added in the 12 months through March 2026 than previously estimated, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics preliminary benchmark revision released on 28 August. The downgrade was driven entirely by the private sector.

The University of Michigan final consumer sentiment index for August fell to 51.7 from 55.2 in July. One-year inflation expectations eased to 4% from 4.2%, below the 4.3% consensus, while five-year expectations held at 3.3%.
The mix of softer labour data and sticky price expectations frames a heavy data run into the 16 September FOMC meeting, including an August CPI report due five days before the decision.

crypto-macro.h3: Chicago PMI collapses to 47.1 from 57.6
crypto-macro.summary: The regional factory gauge missed a forecast of 57 by a wide margin on 28 August, though markets largely looked past it.
body: 47.1 was the August Chicago PMI reading, down from 57.6 in July and far below the 57 economists expected. Readings under 50 signal contraction.
The print landed minutes before the Jackson Hole keynote and drew little reaction. The national ISM manufacturing survey follows on Tuesday.

crypto-macro.h3: Bessent doubles Treasury buybacks as long yields resist
crypto-macro.summary: The buyback ceiling for 10-year to 30-year debt went from $2 billion to at least $4 billion, but yields erased the drop within a day.
body: $4 billion is the new floor for Treasury liquidity support buyback operations in the 10-year to 30-year sector, double the previous $2 billion maximum. The Treasury announced the change on 19 August.

Yields fell on the news, with the 10-year note closing down 5.7 basis points at 4.647% and the 30-year bond down 9 basis points at 5.196%. Less than 24 hours later both had retraced past their pre-announcement levels, prompting Secretary Scott Bessent to say operations could run larger than $4 billion per issue.

Bessent has built the Treasury General Account to roughly $950 billion, a pool that could fund larger purchases. Warsh has argued the market should set long rates, which puts Treasury and the Fed on quietly different tracks.

crypto-macro.h3: El-Erian calls 60% September hike odds too high
crypto-macro.summary: The former Pimco chief argued market-based inflation expectations remain anchored and that hikes would hit rate-sensitive sectors.
body: 60% odds of a September rate hike are too high, Mohamed El-Erian said on the afternoon of 28 August, hours after markets repriced from roughly 35%.

He argued that market-based measures of inflation expectations remain well anchored, that AI-driven productivity gains give reason for optimism about the supply side and that AI demand-side worries are likely to abate.
El-Erian added that hikes would land hardest on already struggling interest-rate-sensitive sectors such as housing.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin slides below $78,000 as Jackson Hole bites
crypto-macro.summary: BTC gave up a move above $81,000 and crypto equities fell sharply after the hawkish keynote on 28 August.
body: $78,000 was breached on the downside on 28 August as bitcoin fell 3.2% over 24 hours, having traded above $81,000 overnight. The token had opened the day at $80,261.86, up 1.5% on Thursday.

Gold dipped and then recovered to above $4,550 an ounce, the dollar index edged up to 99.5 and the front end of the Treasury curve sold off while the 30-year yield eased to about 5.15%. German 10-year yields hit a fresh high of 3.28%.
By Sunday bitcoin had recovered to near $78,900, up more than 2.5% from the Friday low.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin options worth $6.4 billion expire on Deribit
crypto-macro.summary: About 81,700 contracts settled on 28 August, clearing positioning built before bitcoin surged more than 20% in a week.
body: 81,700 contracts worth roughly $6.4 billion expired on Deribit at 08:00 UTC on 28 August, one of the largest bitcoin options expiries of the year.

Most of that positioning was set before bitcoin climbed from around $62,000 to near $80,000 in a week. By Thursday the rally had pushed the price into heavy clusters of bets at $75,000 and $80,000, while the max pain level where the largest number of options expire worthless sat far lower at about $68,000 to $70,000.
The settlement removes those expiring positions, so the next distribution of open interest reflects where traders are placing bets after the move rather than before it.

crypto-macro.h3: Saylor hints at first Strategy bitcoin buy since June
crypto-macro.summary: A two-word post from the Strategy chairman suggested the company resumed accumulation as bitcoin dominance climbed above 60%.
body: 22 June was the last confirmed Strategy bitcoin purchase before executive chairman Michael Saylor posted the words We are Back on X on 30 August, with bitcoin trading near $79,000.

Strategy had spent recent months selling some of its bitcoin to shore up its balance sheet, then switched to selling MSTR shares to raise about $2 billion in dollar reserves and began buying back its STRC preferred stock. The preferred traded as high as $98 on Friday against a $100 reference level.
Bitcoin dominance has risen by almost 4% from its June low to above 60%, a signal of relative strength against the rest of the crypto market. Strategy shares closed at $127.31.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin ETF inflows top $3 billion in best month of 2026
crypto-macro.summary: US spot bitcoin funds logged eight straight days of net inflows through 27 August, roughly double the April total.
body: $3 billion is the August tally for US spot bitcoin ETFs, already the strongest month of 2026 and roughly double what April managed.
The run reached eight consecutive days of net inflows by 27 August, the session when bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 while software stocks led a broader equity rally.

The contrast with the spring is sharp. Bitcoin funds suffered a record 10-day outflow streak from 15 May after April CPI printed at 3.8%, the highest since May 2023, which revived higher-for-longer rate pricing.

crypto-macro.h3: Decade-old bitcoin wallets moved $40 million in August
crypto-macro.summary: Six wallets untouched for 10 years shifted coins this month, but Galaxy data puts dormant activity at a four-year low.
body: $40 million worth of bitcoin left six wallets that had been untouched for a decade during August, and most of it avoided exchanges.

Galaxy data shows dormant coin activity at its lowest level since 2022, with 2026 on pace for under half of last year total. Long-dormant supply moving to exchanges is one of the signals traders watch for distribution by early holders.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin and Ethereum publish post-quantum migration plans
crypto-macro.summary: Ripple is hardening the XRP Ledger for Q-Day while the two largest chains set out their own quantum plans this week.
body: 67 million is the factor by which an Anthropic model cut the work needed to break a leading post-quantum signature candidate last month, a result that has pushed quantum readiness up the agenda across major chains.

Ripple is preparing the XRP Ledger for the arrival of cryptographically relevant quantum computers, the moment the industry calls Q-Day. Bitcoin and Ethereum published their own migration plans during the same week.
Migration touches signature schemes, wallet formats and every dormant coin whose owner may never move it, so chains have to offer a route to new keys without stranding balances.

crypto-macro.h3: Cronos halts chain after $75 million Tectonic exploit
crypto-macro.summary: An attacker pumped the illiquid TONIC token roughly 100 times, then borrowed against it, forcing the Crypto.com-linked network to stop.
body: $75 million is the estimated damage from an exploit of Tectonic, the largest lending protocol on the Crypto.com-linked Cronos network, according to onchain researcher Weilin Li. Cronos halted the blockchain on 30 August.

Li says the attacker pushed TONIC, the thinly traded governance token, up about 100 times within 20 minutes, then used the inflated tokens as collateral to borrow other assets. Tectonic held roughly $121.7 million in total value locked and about $82.7 million in active loans before the incident, according to DefiLlama.

Only about $6 million reached Ethereum before the halt. Crypto.com chief executive Kris Marsalek said the app and exchange were not compromised and that his security team is assisting. The pattern echoes an $8.7 million attack on Moonwell three days earlier and roughly $36 million of liquidations on Morpho on 25 August.

crypto-macro.h3: Solana passes first network vote to double disinflation
crypto-macro.summary: Proposal SGP-0002 scraped through with 67% support, just above the two-thirds threshold, cutting future SOL issuance.
body: 67% support carried Solana first network-wide governance vote, barely clearing the 66.67% needed to pass. The proposal doubles the annual rate at which Solana inflation declines to 30% from 15%.

That brings issuance down to its 1.5% floor around 2029 instead of 2032 and means roughly 18.9 million fewer SOL created over six years. Kraken and Galaxy-linked validators switched sides late in the count.

SOL bounced as the result firmed then gave the gains back as bitcoin slipped below $78,000, trading around $105 and down 3% on the day. It still ended among the best performing majors for the week with a 12% advance.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitwise fund is first Solana ETF to reach $1 billion
crypto-macro.summary: BSOL crossed the mark on 28 August, about 10 months after launch and holding more than half of all Solana ETF assets.
body: $1 billion in assets under management was crossed by the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF on 28 August, the first Solana fund to get there. It started trading on NYSE Arca on 28 October 2025 with a 0.20% management fee.

The fund held about 9.33 million SOL as of 26 August, worth roughly $1.018 billion, and stakes all of its holdings with network validators to earn protocol rewards. Solana funds as a category hold about $1.7 billion, so BSOL accounts for more than half.
ETF analysts Eric Balchunas and James Seyffart noted that Solana funds have never seen major outflows despite weak performance of the underlying token since launch.

crypto-macro.h3: Fogo halts mainnet after 400 million tokens are drained
crypto-macro.summary: The Layer 1 stopped block production after an attacker received more than 10% of circulating FOGO supply from foundation wallets.
body: 400 million FOGO tokens, more than 10% of circulating supply and worth roughly $3 million at the time, moved to an attacker after the Fogo Foundation was compromised. The chain halted its mainnet on 29 August.

The foundation first said the blockchain was operating normally, then paused it about 15 hours later to stop further movement of the affected assets. Validators were told to upgrade the network to restrict addresses linked to the activity.

Fogo has not disclosed the attack vector or whether private keys were taken, and says it has notified exchanges, law enforcement agencies and forensic specialists. The token fell roughly 18% to 20% after the disclosure.

crypto-macro.h3: Ethena looks to equity perpetuals to back $4 billion USDe
crypto-macro.summary: The issuer expects real-world asset perpetuals to overtake crypto derivatives in USDe backing within one to two years.
body: $4 billion of USDe sits behind Ethena plans to source yield from booming equity perpetual futures rather than only crypto derivatives.

The company said it expects real-world asset perpetuals to eclipse crypto derivatives in the token backing within 12 to 24 months, a shift that would tie a large synthetic dollar to equity market funding rates instead of bitcoin and ether basis.
Trading venues are pushing into the same territory. Bybit launched 24/7 options on stock perpetuals on 28 August, starting with SpaceX and Nvidia.

crypto-macro.h3: Crypto card hack of $1.1 million sinks neobank token 49%
crypto-macro.summary: An exploit of a crypto card programme drove the AVICI token to a record low before it pared some of the losses.
body: $1.1 million was taken in an exploit of a crypto card product on 29 August, and the issuing neobank AVICI token fell 49% from its 24-hour high to a record low before recovering part of the drop.

The incident adds to a run of late-August security failures spanning lending protocols, cross-chain infrastructure and consumer crypto products, with Cronos, Fogo and Cosmos all reporting losses in the same week.

crypto-macro.h3: Ninth Circuit hands Kalshi a loss and splits the courts
crypto-macro.summary: Judges ruled Nevada can apply its gaming rules to Kalshi sports event contracts, contradicting an April ruling in the New Jersey case.
body: A unanimous panel of the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit ruled on 28 August that the Commodity Exchange Act likely does not preempt Nevada gaming regulations as applied to Kalshi sports event contracts, because those contracts were sports bets rather than swaps.

In April a different federal appeals court told New Jersey it had no business regulating Kalshi. A CFTC spokesman said the Ninth Circuit invented a new exception to the statute and that the split calls for Supreme Court resolution. Kalshi said it will seek further review.

Nevada Gaming Control Board chairman Mike Dreitzer said the ruling vindicates the state position. Kalshi had already pulled out of Nevada and other jurisdictions, and Connecticut filed a fresh lawsuit earlier in the week.

crypto-macro.h3: UK to give the Bank of England a stablecoin objective
crypto-macro.summary: Ministers plan a secondary objective on payments innovation and digital money, with annual reporting to Parliament.
body: A new secondary objective for the Bank of England to support innovation in payment systems and digital money such as stablecoins was set out by the British government on 26 August. Financial stability remains the primary duty.

The change would arrive through an amendment to the Financial Services and Markets Bill, which the House of Lords is due to debate on 7 and 9 September. The Bank would report to Parliament each year on how it is advancing innovation.
Britain is separately preparing stablecoin rules that include a temporary £40 billion holding cap for each systemic token.

crypto-macro.h3: ECB says digital euro will offer maximum privacy available
crypto-macro.summary: Executive board member Piero Cipollone pushed back on surveillance fears, saying the Eurosystem cannot link people to transactions.
body: The digital euro guarantees the maximum level of privacy that current technology can offer, ECB executive board member Piero Cipollone said in an interview with Italian outlet ilsussidiario.net published in late August.

Cipollone said the Eurosystem would be structurally unable to link individuals to digital euro transactions online or offline. Commercial banks distributing the currency would still see payments and keep their existing identity and reporting obligations, while offline payments would be visible only to payer and recipient.

The European Parliament agreed its negotiating position in July and talks with member states target a deal by the end of 2026. The ECB has named 36 payment providers, among them Deutsche Bank, UniCredit and Revolut, for a 12-month pilot from the second half of 2027, with first issuance targeted for 2029.

crypto-macro.h3: Clarity Act slips to September as banks build anyway
crypto-macro.summary: The US market structure bill missed another window, leaving banks to make design choices without settled rules.
body: September is the new target for the Clarity Act after the US crypto market structure bill slipped again, a delay picked apart in a CoinDesk opinion piece published on 28 August by Matter Labs policy lead Vassilis Tziokas.

The argument is that banks are already building tokenised infrastructure and that every month without settled rules quietly rewards the walled garden, because closed permissioned systems carry less regulatory ambiguity than open networks.

crypto-macro.h3: Chainalysis protests ICE award of $95 million to TRM Labs
crypto-macro.summary: The blockchain analytics firm says the immigration agency unfairly steered a large tracing contract to a rival vendor.
body: $95 million is the value of the blockchain analytics contract that Chainalysis says US Immigration and Customs Enforcement unfairly steered to competitor TRM Labs. The Block reported the protest on 30 August.

Federal tracing contracts have become a meaningful revenue line for the small group of firms that sell blockchain surveillance to law enforcement, which makes the terms of individual awards consequential for the sector.

mental-health.h3: Americans say chatbots hurt more than help on loneliness
mental-health.summary: A Pew survey of 3,488 US adults published on 25 August found scepticism strongest among people under 30.
body: 39% of US adults say chatbots do more to hurt people who use them for loneliness against 19% who say they do more to help, according to a Pew Research Center report published on 25 August.

For depression the split was 36% hurt against 17% help, and for stress it was 29% against 22%. The centre surveyed 3,488 adults from 22 to 28 June 2026 through its American Trends Panel of randomly selected US adults.

Adults under 30 were the most sceptical, with 49% saying chatbots hurt on loneliness and 41% saying the same on depression, and 23% saying they help on each. Among adults 65 and older, four in ten or more said they were not sure either way.

mental-health.h3: APA finds 77% of psychologists see patients using AI
mental-health.summary: More than 1,200 licensed clinicians described how patients bring chatbots into therapy, and 94% doubt bots can handle clinical nuance.
body: 77% of licensed psychologists have spoken with patients who used AI for support or engagement, according to an American Psychological Association survey of more than 1,200 clinicians directly involved in patient care.

More than a third report patients treating AI as an additional mental health professional, and 34% have patients using it for self-discipline, affirmations or behavioural reminders. The survey ran online from 9 to 26 April 2026.

94% said chatbots cannot treat mental health conditions with the appropriate level of nuance. The association frames AI as a tool to be used carefully rather than a substitute for a qualified provider.

mental-health.h3: Nearly one in five young Americans ask AI for mental health advice
mental-health.summary: A JAMA Pediatrics research letter found 19.2% of adolescents and young adults used chatbots for mental health advice in 2025, and most told nobody.
body: 19.2% of US adolescents and young adults reported using AI chatbots for mental health advice in 2025, according to a JAMA Pediatrics research letter built on RAND survey work.
Among those who did, 42.8% sought advice at least monthly and 91.7% rated what they got as somewhat or very helpful. 63.3% had not disclosed the use to anyone.

Use among people aged 12 to 21 rose by more than 40% over the previous year. The non-disclosure finding matters clinically because it means treating clinicians and parents often have no visibility into a source the young person is relying on.

mental-health.h3: SAMHSA issues federal policy paper on AI in mental health
mental-health.summary: The August paper reviews current evidence and sets out considerations for policymakers governing AI in mental health and substance use services.
body: August 2026 is the publication date on SAMHSA policy paper PEP26-01-003, which reviews current evidence on artificial intelligence in mental health services and was posted on 19 August.

The paper examines what is known and what is proposed across a fast-moving AI landscape, then sets out considerations for policymakers responsible for governing its advance into mental health and substance use disorder services.

It is aimed at policymakers, professional care providers and public health professionals, and sits alongside a separate SAMHSA advisory on how wearables and other digital tools are being used in behavioural health.

mental-health.h3: Researchers urge chatbot safety be judged across whole conversations
mental-health.summary: A JMIR Mental Health paper argues single end-point tests miss how exchanges drift and calls for trajectory-based evaluation instead.
body: Endpoints are the wrong unit of analysis for chatbot mental health safety, argue the authors of a 2026 JMIR Mental Health paper on moving from end points to trajectories.

Large language models are now embedded in everyday life through chatbots people use for practical assistance, companionship and support with mental health and emotional wellbeing. The authors argue safety should be measured across the arc of an exchange rather than at one sampled moment, because risk can emerge gradually.

mental-health.h3: People with depression set their own conditions for AI chatbots
mental-health.summary: A qualitative study with 17 participants found users want actionable information, validation with clear limits and no unsafe data disclosure.
body: 17 people with lived experience of depression interacted with a GPT-4o based chatbot called Zenny for a JMIR Mental Health qualitative study, then sat for interviews about what worked and what did not.

Participants described three intertwined priorities: actionable information, emotional validation with clear limits and personalisation that does not require handing over unsafe amounts of personal data.
The authors translate those into concrete design strategies to mitigate harm and position LLM-based tools as complements to human support and recovery rather than replacements for them.

mental-health.h3: Survey of 1,805 adults maps AI mental health help-seeking
mental-health.summary: A JMIR Mental Health cross-sectional study examined how 18 to 49 year olds use generative AI and how they rank it against human professionals.
body: 1,805 US adults aged 18 to 49 answered an anonymous online survey in October 2025 about using generative AI and AI-assisted mental health chatbots as mental health resources.

The study, published in JMIR Mental Health in 2026, also measured how respondents rank these tools relative to human mental health professionals, a comparison that matters as access and cost push people toward whatever is available at 2am.

mental-health.h3: Sword Health moves to buy Headspace in all-cash deal
mental-health.summary: A state regulatory filing revealed the acquisition, reported at $200 million to $300 million and due to take effect on 14 September.
body: $200 million to $300 million in cash is the reported price for Sword Health acquisition of Headspace, a deal that surfaced through a state regulatory filing rather than a company announcement. STAT reported it on 25 August.

Headspace notified the Massachusetts Health Policy Commission on 22 July that its parent OrangeDot proposed to be acquired through a merger with a Sword subsidiary. The transaction is due to take effect on 14 September.

The price marks a steep markdown from the roughly $3 billion valuation Headspace carried in 2021. Sword started in AI-driven virtual physical therapy and has since expanded into women's health, cardiometabolic care and mental health.

mental-health.h3: Talkspace pitches Tee as a safer consumer mental health bot
mental-health.summary: The AI guide launched in June 2026, was built on about 450 million therapy-related data points and escalates flagged conversations to clinicians.
body: 450 million therapy-related pieces of data went into Tee, the AI mental health guide Talkspace launched in early June 2026. Chief executive Jon Cohen says it functions as a conversational agent, is not therapy and does not diagnose.

Algorithms flag major risks including suicide, homicide and substance use, and can pick up evidence of delusion, mania, hallucinations, disorganised thinking, eating disorders or obsessive-compulsive disorder. Flagged conversations escalate to a live clinician who decides whether intervention is needed.

Tee is free for a first week then costs $19.99 a month, and Talkspace has started talking to payers about coverage and to employers about assistance programmes. Universal Health Services recently closed its roughly $835 million acquisition of Talkspace, which gives the tool a distribution channel.

mental-health.h3: Colorado AI therapy ban takes effect as five states restrict bots
mental-health.summary: Five states enacted AI therapy restrictions in 2026, joining Illinois and Nevada, with most relying on professional licensing powers.
body: 12 August 2026 is when Colorado law prohibiting AI therapy chatbots took effect, one of five state restrictions enacted this year according to the Transparency Coalition mid-year legislation report.

Maine took effect on 29 July and treats unlicensed AI therapy as an unfair trade practice. Tennessee took effect on 1 July and bars systems that advertise or represent themselves as qualified mental health professionals. Vermont took effect on 17 June and Rhode Island follows on 1 January 2027.
The bans lean largely on state authority to license mental health professionals rather than on technology regulation. Illinois and Nevada adopted comparable measures last year.

mental-health.h3: Precise Behavioral raises $14.2 million for hospital AI tools
mental-health.summary: The physician-led company targets emergency department boarding with virtual psychiatry, on-demand consults and AI-driven software.
body: $14.2 million in venture funding went to Precise Behavioral, announced on 29 July and led by A1 Health Ventures with Ziegler Link-Age Fund, Converge Capital Partners and Granite Financial Holdings, an affiliate of Blue Cross of Idaho.

Founded in 2022 by Dr Nitin Nanda, the company sells virtual psychiatry, on-demand consults and billing tools to hospitals dealing with mental health patients stuck in emergency departments. It says it is already profitable and will use the money to scale operations and its AI roadmap.
Before the round it had agreements with four California health systems covering 200 hospitals, 30,000 beds, 100,000 providers and 24 million patients.

mental-health.h3: FDA scales back oversight of low-risk AI health software
mental-health.summary: January guidance narrowed which AI-enabled tools need clearance while the agency keeps a separate focus on generative AI mental health devices.
body: 1,300 is the number of AI-enabled medical devices the FDA has now cleared across diagnostics, chronic disease management, mental health and remote monitoring.

Guidance published in January 2026 reduced oversight of certain digital health products including AI-enabled software and wearables. Clinician-support tools that summarise patient data or suggest options for a clinician to evaluate independently may fall outside clearance requirements. The agency has also run a TEMPO pilot with CMS to route digital health devices to Medicare and Medicaid patients.

Generative AI mental health devices remain a separate track. The FDA Digital Health Advisory Committee met in November 2025 specifically on that category, following an inaugural session a year earlier, with attention on content controls, privacy and unreported suicidal ideation.
